candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture (multiloculated cystic lesion, mucinous fluid and membranes, negative CEA/CA markers, young woman) is inconsistent with cholangiocarcinoma, which is a solid/infiltrative malignancy. The reference diagnosis is a benign hepatic cystadenoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cholangiocarcinoma is a malignant biliary neoplasm; the reference is hepatic cystadenoma, a benign cystic neoplasm

candidate_relations.scope_detail: Includes both cystadenoma and cystadenocarcinoma; the reference specifies only the benign cystadenoma without malignant component

candidate_relations.reason: Biliary cystadenoma and hepatic cystadenoma refer to the same entity—a benign multiloculated mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver arising from biliary epithelium. All clinical features (young North African woman, multiloculated cyst, mucinous fluid and membranes, biliary communication, negative serology) are consistent. The term 'biliary' specifies the epithelial origin without conflicting with 'hepatic' as a location descriptor.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Biliary cystadenoma is a recognized synonym/alias for hepatic cystadenoma arising from biliary epithelium

candidate_relations.reason: Although IPMN of the bile duct can produce mucin and biliary obstruction, it is classified as a separate neoplastic entity (intraductal growth pattern, papillary architecture) rather than a cystic hepatic parenchymal lesion. The reference diagnosis is hepatic cystadenoma, which is a parenchymal cystic neoplasm with biliary communication, not a primary intraductal papillary neoplasm.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: IPMN of the bile duct is a distinct entity (intraductal papillary neoplasm) separate from hepatic/biliary cystadenoma

case_quality_flags: Hepatic cystadenoma and biliary cystadenoma are used interchangeably in the literature; C003 is accepted as complete equivalent
